  • Sunil Mittal says Bharti Group open to raising OneWeb stake to 30%, rules out majority control

    In a bold move, Bharti Group plans to elevate its position in Eutelsat OneWeb to roughly 30%. The organization seeks to uphold its European identity in the satellite industry. Sunil Bharti Mittal shared ambitious plans, such as entering financial services and establishing AI data centers. He also highlights the crucial task of developing a leadership transition plan, stressing the importance of prioritizing the enterprise over family dynamics in strategic decisions.

    US returns over $12 billion in oil proceeds to Venezuela since Maduro's ouster, report says

    The Trump administration has reported returning over $12 billion in oil revenue to Venezuela as of September 30. Almost all funds from oil sales have been directed to support infrastructure and humanitarian needs. The U.S. Treasury managed the escrow account from which these funds were disbursed following approved requests. Various payments were made for essential supplies and services, including healthcare-related equipment.

    Banks seek centralised fraud reporting mechanism ahead of RBI compensation policy

    Banks have approached the Reserve Bank of India seeking clarity on customer eligibility, reporting timelines and liability-sharing under its compensation framework for victims of small-value fraudulent electronic transactions. The policy, set to take effect in January 2027, provides eligible customers compensation of up to ₹25,000, with RBI and banks sharing the cost.

    Smaller MFIs change tack: No onlending, just routing funds

    India’s microfinance sector is seeing a structural shift as funding constraints and mounting stress push smaller lenders away from direct lending towards business correspondent models. With bank funding and fresh equity drying up, lenders are increasingly pursuing off-balance-sheet growth and earning fee income by acting as agents for banks. Industry leaders say the traditional joint-liability group lending model is losing relevance as borrowers gain access to multiple formal and digital credit options.

    Singapore Airlines keeps faith in Air India turnaround efforts

    Singapore Airlines has backed Air India CEO Tewolde Gebremariam’s turnaround efforts, while cautioning that the 16% decline in its share of Air India’s losses in the September half was largely due to a reversal of earlier provisions rather than an improvement in the airline’s financial performance. Air India is exploring aircraft conversions into freighters to tap India’s underpenetrated air cargo market, while also seeking to expand overseas ticket sales and improve network efficiency.

    PE firm Advent shortlists buyers to sell stake in 'Crax' maker DFM Foods

    Advent International has shortlisted Partners Group, ChrysCapital and EQT to sell its 96.63% stake in Crax maker DFM Foods, with ITC and Goldman Sachs also in contention at a valuation of ₹4,000-4,200 crore. Balaji Wafers and other strategic bidders have exited amid concerns over the steep valuation.

    Tata Steel's UK operations seen recovering from March quarter

    Tata Steel expects its UK operations to move towards profitability in the March quarter as excess imported steel inventories ease, while its Netherlands business is projected to improve in the second half. CEO T V Narendran said strong infrastructure spending and automobile demand continue to support India's steel business, with domestic performance expected to improve in H2.

Global bond yields surge to multi-year highs as inflation, borrowing concerns mount

Government bond yields globally rose to multi-decade highs recently due to sell-offs in sovereign debt. Investors demanded higher returns amid persistent inflation and uncertainty regarding interest rates. India's benchmark 10-year bond yield peaked at 7.50% before slightly declining to 7.24%. Recent easing geopolitical tensions and declining crude prices have supported bond market recovery. Nonetheless, the outlook remains uncertain due to inflationary pressures and concerns over fiscal sustainability.

UAE: 14 killed, 30 injured after truck crashes into vehicles in Fujairah; Indians among hurt

At least 14 people were killed and 30 injured, including Indian nationals, after a truck rammed into several vehicles on a road in the UAE's Fujairah emirate, triggering a fire. Fujairah Police said 15 injured people had been discharged from hospitals, while the remaining victims continued to receive treatment.

Visa barriers push students from US and UK to Asia and Europe, global survey shows

International students are shifting their preferences towards universities in Asia and Europe rather than traditional destinations. The survey indicates a significant decline in enrolment numbers in the US and Britain due to recent policy changes. Visa restrictions and government policies are identified as the primary barriers impacting international student enrolment rates. Additionally, universities in Canada and Australia also witnessed weaker demand during this time.

Migration to developed countries declines for second year: OECD

Migration to developed countries experienced a decline of 1.6 percent in 2025 compared to 2024. Many Western nations faced backlash against irregular migrants due to conflict and economic hardships. Legal humanitarian migration saw a significant drop of 26 percent, while labour migration increased by 13 percent. Portugal, Spain, and Italy noted substantial increases in permanent migrants, while the United States and Canada saw decreases.

US proposes tougher H-1B visa extension scrutiny and over 2 lakh foreign worker petitions could be affected annually

The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has proposed removing a rule that requires immigration officers to give weight to previous approvals when reviewing certain work visa extension applications. The change could affect around 208,429 petitions annually, including H-1B, L-1, O-1, TN and E visa categories. If finalised, the proposal would allow USCIS officers to reassess applications even when workers remain with the same employer in unchanged roles.
